characters.summary: Ulmo is the Vala of the waters of Arda, operating through the oceans, rivers, and deep waters. He does not dwell in Valinor but moves unseen through the depths of the world, offering counsel and wielding immense elemental authority over water.
mobility: Movement through all waters of the world
limitations: Bound to act according to Eru's design; lacks physical form in Valinor and interacts mostly through water or visions.

sources.supports: Ulmo's role as Lord of Waters and Vala in Tolkien's legendarium.

feats.claim: Wielded immense power over the waters of Arda, causing the sea to rise and terrifying the armies of Morgoth.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of Tuor and the Fall of Gondolin

campaignTags.claim: Ulmo is the Lord of Waters and rules the oceans and rivers of Arda.
Ulmo dwells in the deep waters of the ocean.

unknowns: Exact physical combat capabilities outside of environmental water manipulation.

characters.summary: Ungoliant is a primordial spirit of monstrous spider form who hungers for light and weaves dark webs of unlight. She drains the life and radiance from objects and beings, growing to terrifying size.

mechanisms: Cloaking herself and targets in impenetrable darkness (Unlight)

weaknesses: Extreme hunger that can never be satisfied, eventually leading her to consume herself.
limitations: Power depends on consuming light; vulnerable to immense sustained forces when starved.

sources.supports: Ungoliant's nature, her alliance with Melkor, and her draining of the Two Trees.

feats.claim: Drank the sap of the Two Trees of Valinor, destroying them and blinding the realm.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Darkening of Valinor

feats.claim: Overpowered Melkor in physical combat when he attempted to withhold the Silmarils.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Flight of the Noldor

notableResults.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Flight of the Noldor
notableResults.note: Pinned Melkor down with her webs when he tried to cheat her out of the Silmarils, forced to retreat only when Melkor's Balrogs rescued him.

campaignTags.claim: Ungoliant grew to a monstrous, colossal spider size after drinking the sap of the Two Trees.

unknowns: The ultimate origin of Ungoliant before she came to Arda.

characters.summary: Vairë the Weaver is one of the Valier, wife of Mandos. She weaves all things that have ever been in Time into her ever-expanding tapestries that line the halls of Mandos.

techniques: Weaving the tapestry of Time and history

limitations: Does not engage in direct combat or worldly interference.

sources.supports: Vairë's description as the weaver of time and wife of Mandos in Valinor.

feats.claim: Weaves the tapestries of all events in the history of Arda within the Halls of Mandos.

unknowns: Any direct offensive or combat feats.

characters.summary: Vána the Ever-young is one of the Valier, younger sister of Yavanna. She is associated with flowers, golden birds, and the blossoming of spring across Arda.

techniques: Blessing flora and fauna with perpetual renewal

limitations: Does not engage in combat or martial actions.

sources.supports: Vána's status as Queen of flowers and living things, wife of Oromë.

feats.claim: Causes flowers to spring up and birds to sing at her passing in the gardens of Valinor.

characters.summary: Varda, also known as Elbereth, is the Queen of the Valar and spouse of Manwë. She kindled the stars and holds immense power over light, inspiring deep reverence and fear in creatures of darkness.

techniques: Blinding or searing light projection against darkness

mechanisms: Supreme angelic authority and celestial radiance

limitations: Rarely descends into direct physical conflicts, acting chiefly through cosmic ordinance and divine authority.

sources.supports: Varda's identity as Queen of the Valar, creator of the stars, and opponent of Melkor.

feats.claim: Created the stars of Valinor and the greater constellations to combat Melkor's darkness.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Beginning of Days

feats.claim: Refused Melkor entry and filled him with terror due to her mastery over light.

campaignTags.claim: Varda moves through the skies of Arda.

unknowns: Direct combat engagements on a tactical battlefield.

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings / The Silmarillion
characters.summary: The Witch-king is the chief of the Nazgûl, Sauron's most powerful servants. He wields terror, dark sorcery, a fiery blade, and a Morgul-knife, dominating foes through psychological dread and lethal martial skill.

techniques: Black breath (aura of terror and despair)

mechanisms: Wraith form immune to ordinary mortal weapons
Magical protection ('No man may slay him')

weaknesses: Vulnerable to blessed weapons (e.g., Westernesse blades) and special prophecies ('not by the hand of man will he fall').
limitations: Physical form is sustained by Sauron's will and rings; weak against sunlight when unmasked in lesser forms, though powerful at full night.

sources.supports: The Witch-king's identity, weapons, status as leader of the Nazgûl, and death by Éowyn and Merry.

feats.claim: Stabbed Frodo Baggins with a Morgul-knife on Weathertop.
feats.citation: The Fellowship of the Ring, Flight to the Ford

feats.claim: Broke the great gates of Minas Tirith using Grond combined with spells of ruin.
feats.citation: The Return of the King, The Siege of Gondor

feats.claim: Paralyzed Gandalf the White with fear and dark power before the gates of Minas Tirith.
feats.citation: The Return of the King, The Siege of Gondor

notableResults.citation: The Return of the King, The Battle of the Pelennor Fields
notableResults.note: Slain after Merry struck him with a Barrow-blade (breaking his magical defenses) and Éowyn delivered the fatal blow.

campaignTags.claim: The Witch-king uses dark sorcery to break the gates of Minas Tirith.
The Witch-king wields a fiery sword.
The Witch-king rides a winged fell beast into battle.

unknowns: Exact mechanics of his resistance to standard magic.

characters.summary: Yavanna the Giver of Fruits is the Vala responsible for all growing things, plants, and animals in Arda. She created the Two Trees of Valinor and conceived the Ents to protect forests.
limitations: Does not engage in martial battle or combat deployment.

sources.supports: Yavanna's identity as Vala of earth, agriculture, and creator of the Two Trees and Ents.

feats.claim: Sang the Two Trees of Valinor into being, creating the prime source of light before the sun and moon.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Beginning of Days

feats.claim: Conceived the Ents as tree-shepherds to guard the forests against the axes of Dwarves and Orcs.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of Aulë and Yavanna

campaignTags.claim: Yavanna sang the Two Trees of Valinor into existence through high song.

unknowns: Direct combat application of her botanical powers.
